newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to reduce Statfjord field output.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to reduce Statfjord field output.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Wednesday it expected to start reducing production at the North Sea Statfjord oilfield late on Thursday due to forecasts of bad weather.
Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said one shuttle tanker continued to load at the Statfjord A platform at 1320 GMT, but there were no more vessels in the area.
"That ship will continue to load until the captain says to stop. The waves are getting higher and the forecasts are expecting storms," Steihaug told Reuters.
She said throughput at Statfjord B and C would be reduced from midnight on Thursday and Statfjord A would cut output six hours later.
Gullfaks had enough storage capacity to remain in full production for another 48 hours.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrel per day (bpd) and processes crude from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre and Vigdis developments, which in total add roughly 400,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 85,000 bpd of output from the Tordis field.
